newsitem.title: UK: Weather for US winter wheat seen reverse of 1995.
newsitem.headline: Weather for US winter wheat seen reverse of 1995.

text.p: The weather situation for US winter wheat going into this winter is "almost a complete reversal of last year", says Chicago-based Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis. Davis's Winter 1996-97 Winter Outlook was available in London where he addressed an oil conference this week. He said precipitation in the heart of the winter wheat belt had been significantly above normal in the past few months. Much of western Kansas had had 200 percent of normal. "Thus, the crop will go into dormancy this winter in much better shape than it was a year ago", he said. It very hard to assess prospects for winterkill damage as this would depend on how much snow cover there would be. But "early prospects for the hard red winter wheat crop are excellent for a total turnaround from a year ago". Davis also said early rainfall prospects for next spring looked as if they would benefit the soft red crop.
